title: Aggregation and Grouping: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Aggregation and Grouping: Visual Guide

1. Grain Changer | eight retrieval_runs rows partitioned into groups under four different GROUP BY choices, with the NULL bucket marked | GROUP BY collapses rows to one per group and the grain is the combination of the keys, and unlike a join all NULLs form one group together

2. Aggregates Meet NULL | six aggregates walked over the same four rows, one unmeasured, plus a slider that makes the whole group NULL | COUNT(*) counts rows while COUNT(x), SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip NULLs, so AVG is SUM(x)/COUNT(x), and an all-NULL group returns 0 for counts but NULL for values

3. Before Or After | two predicates placed on either side of the collapse, with the pipeline and the version A/B latency numbers recomputed | WHERE filters rows before groups exist and HAVING filters computed groups, and the placement decides which population the metric describes

4. The Set Problem | COUNT(*), COUNT(col) and COUNT(DISTINCT col) over four rows showing which each reads, plus a retention slider comparing summed daily distinct users to the true monthly figure | COUNT DISTINCT is a set-construction problem rather than a slower count, and distinct counts are non-additive across overlapping groups

5. The Arbitrary Column | the MAX(score) with a bare document_id query run by a strict engine and by a permissive one, with four repairs by intent | aggregates operate independently, so a permissive engine can return a document and score pair that never existed in the data
